tasks.spec:
Create a NEW ES-module file worker_cat.js — a sleeping GUILD CAT with pet interaction for the existing 2D guild client. DO NOT rewrite the client: worker_visitor.js (injected below) is your PATTERN — it is a proven working module for this exact client; copy its conventions (state object, install block, update/draw hooks, guards). worker_office.js (also injected) is REFERENCE ONLY for the drawing conventions (iso projection, tile math, fitText, palette).

Your output is ONLY the new file. It must be a self-installing ES module with no imports, safe to node --check (no top-level DOM access; wrap all window/document use in typeof guards or inside functions).

Contract with the client (all on window): V (V.gameState is 'title' or 'play'; V.weather; V.grid {originX, originY, tileW, tileH}; V.camera {x, y, zoom}), iso(gx, gy) -> {x, y} world coords for tile coords, window.GuildVisitor (the playable visitor: {gx, gy, moving, dialogue}), window.cue(name) sound hook if present.

BEHAVIOR:
1. On import: if window.GuildCat is undefined, create window.GuildCat = { gx: 1.8, gy: 3.6, state: 'sleep', stateT: 0, petCount: 0, cooldown: 0, hearts: [], bubble: null, lastBreath: 0 } and attach update and draw functions onto it (window.GuildCat.update = update; window.GuildCat.draw = draw;). Also attach __probe = function () { return { state: GuildCat-state, petCount, hearts: hearts.length }; } for testing. Position the cat curled near the south-east floor area (around tile gx 1.8, gy 3.6) — do not sit on a building tile.
2. update(now): if window.V is undefined or V.gameState !== 'play', return. Cat states: 'sleep' (breathing — body slowly scales, tail flicks every few seconds), 'alert' (sits up if window.GuildVisitor exists and is within 1.5 tiles — ears up, eyes open), 'petted' (if visitor is within 1.2 tiles AND visitor pressed the E key this frame — detect via a keydown listener you attach for 'e'/'E', setting a one-shot flag; on pet: state 'petted' for 2.5s, spawn 5 floating hearts, set bubble 'prrrrr...' for 2s, call window.cue('meow') if typeof window.cue === 'function' inside try/catch, petCount += 1, cooldown 4s before next pet). After 'petted' or visitor leaving, return to sleep.
3. draw(ctx): if window.V undefined or V.gameState !== 'play', return. Draw the cat with iso(gx, gy): curled gray body (main color #9ca3af, darker outline #6b7280, lighter chest), closed-eye arcs when sleeping, small triangle ears, tail curling along the ground; when alert, ears up + open eyes (dark pixels); hearts are red #f87171 pixel hearts floating up and fading (rise 0.5 px/frame, life 1.2s, alternate slight x drift); bubble = small dark rounded rect with #d4af37 border and white text, same style as the visitor dialogue box. Keep all drawing in pixel-art spirit (fillRect-based, no images, no gradients).
4. Everything must run without exceptions even if GuildVisitor is absent (cat just sleeps forever) or cue is absent.

OUTPUT FORMAT: the complete file, wrapped in one standard fenced code block (three backticks, no language tag). No prose outside the fence except one line naming the file.

tasks.spec:
Create a NEW ES-module file worker_trail.js — a footstep TRAIL effect layer for the playable visitor in the existing 2D guild client. worker_visitor.js (injected) is your PATTERN (proven module, copy its conventions). worker_office.js (injected) is REFERENCE ONLY for drawing conventions.

Your output is ONLY the new file: self-installing ES module, no imports, node --check-safe (typeof guards, no top-level DOM).

Contract (all on window): V (V.gameState, V.weather with values like 'CLEAR' or 'RAIN'), iso(gx, gy) -> {x, y}, window.GuildVisitor {gx, gy, moving, facing, walkFrame}.

BEHAVIOR:
1. On import: if window.GuildTrail undefined, create it with { steps: [], lastDrop: 0, side: 0 } and attach update/draw/__probe (__probe returns { steps: steps.length }).
2. update(now): guard on window.V and V.gameState === 'play' and window.GuildVisitor. If the visitor is moving and now - lastDrop > 180 (ms), drop a footprint step at the visitor's current tile position: { x: visitor.gx, y: visitor.gy, side: (side alternates 0/1), t: now, kind }. kind = 'splash' if V.weather === 'RAIN' else 'print'. Cap steps at 40 (drop oldest). Prune steps older than 1200 ms.
3. draw(ctx): guard as above. For each step, project p = iso(step.x, step.y) and draw a small footprint: for 'print' a dark translucent oval (rgba(20,24,32,0.35), about 5x3 px) offset perpendicular to travel direction by side (+/- 2.5 px alternating left/right foot); for 'splash' a light-blue ring (#93c5fd, alpha fading with age) that expands 3px over its life. Alpha of every step fades linearly from 0.6 to 0 across its 1200 ms life. Draw steps oldest first so newer ones overlap older.
4. Zero exceptions if GuildVisitor is absent (no steps ever spawn) or weather string is unknown (treat as 'print').

OUTPUT FORMAT: the complete file in one standard fenced code block (three backticks, no language tag). One line of prose max outside the fence.

tasks.spec:
Create a NEW ES-module file worker_boat.js — a periodic SKY-BOAT COURIER event for the existing 2D guild client: an airship crosses the sky, docks at the island edge, a hooded courier walks to worker 0, delivers a scroll quoting a real tick line, then departs. worker_visitor.js (injected) is your PATTERN (proven module). worker_office.js (injected) is REFERENCE ONLY (iso projection, world/sky drawing, speech-bubble style, palette #d4af37 gold accents on #0d1324).

Your output is ONLY the new file: self-installing ES module, no imports, node --check-safe.

Contract (all on window): V (V.gameState, V.workers — array of worker metadata, V.workers[0].recent_ticks — array of strings, the newest last; V.workerStates[0] {x, y} world position of worker 0), iso(gx, gy) -> {x, y}, window.cue(name) optional sound hook (names: 'done', 'levelup', 'grow', 'alert').

BEHAVIOR — a state machine on window.GuildBoat = { phase: 'idle', t: 0, boatX, courier: {...}, delivery: null, dockX, dockY } with update/draw/__probe attached (probe returns { phase, delivery }).
1. idle: wait 20 s (use a phase timer), then pick dock point at the island's east edge in the SKY area (world coords: derive from iso of tile gx 6.5, gy -1.5 — above/right of the island, inside the canvas) and enter approach.
2. approach: airship sprite (pixel-art: dark violet hull #3b3358 with gold #d4af37 trim, small propeller circle at the rear that spins — alternate two frames every 150 ms, a hanging lantern, rope ladder coiled) flies from off-screen left toward the dock point at steady speed (ease into dock over ~4 s). On arrival: cue('alert') if cue exists (try/catch), phase docked.
3. docked: rope ladder unrolls (simple line + rungs) and the HOODED COURIER descends it (violet robe #8b5cf6 like step5, face hidden — dark hood), then walks (4-frame walk like the visitor pattern) from the dock point toward worker 0's world position, stopping 24 px away. Face worker 0. Show a scroll-delivery bubble in the visitor dialogue style: gold border, dark box, text = a REAL quote from V.workers[0].recent_ticks (use the newest string, trimmed to 80 chars; if the array is missing or empty use 'A courier hands you a fresh dispatch.'). Hold 6 s, then phase depart.
4. depart: courier walks back to the ladder, climbs (moves up along the rope), boat accelerates off-screen right, then phase idle with a fresh 20-30 s random-ish timer (Math.random).
5. update(now) guards on window.V && V.gameState === 'play' — when not 'play', freeze the phase timer (do not advance t). draw(ctx) guards the same and draws boat, ladder, courier, and bubble. Bubble must use measured-width text and a clip region so nothing spills.

OUTPUT FORMAT: the complete file in one standard fenced code block (three backticks, no language tag). One line of prose max outside the fence.
